text:
soren: Quick follow-up from the RFC — proposal to shift enforcement of region/data-residency decisions into the control plane and make edge routers lightweight policy-followers. Idea is: control plane holds authoritative residency map + routing policy; routers accept an immutable header from control-plane that drives routing, and fall back to simple local heuristics if header is missing. Tradeoffs: simpler router, easier private deploys, but control-plane becomes more critical in failover paths. Thoughts? :thinking:

anika: Question — how do we handle KMS/HSM boundaries? If control plane issues a routing header but cannot access region-specific keys, we risk illegal cross-border decrypts. Do we require per-region KMS proxies or key mirroring?

jeff: Also worried about in-flight requests. If control plane flips a tenant to a different region, existing sessions pinned to GPU pools elsewhere could get dropped. We need a drain/grace mechanism and an idempotent request retry path.

rachel: Suggest operator tooling for scheduled cutovers and an explicit manual pin. Add a "cutover-mode: staged" option so we can canary traffic (e.g. 1%) before full cutover. Operator UI should show current residency decision + active drainer state. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: canary-test: control-plane -> router signing ok; router fallback tests passed (small sample). logs: https://ci.example/test/1715305100 :white_check_mark:

maria: Operational scale question — do we make the control plane globally active with region-affine replicas (leader per-region) or keep a single global leader? Leader election complexity is non-trivial for fast cutovers.

soren: sketch of runtime header + simple config we discussed:
```
X-Region-Hint: eu-west-1
router.policy.fallback = "local-prefer"
router.cache.kv_ttl = 30s
controlplane.cutover.canary_pct = 1
```
Router only reads the signed header from control-plane; cache TTL short so we don't saturate control-plane on cutover. Drain window scheduled when header changes.

anika: For KMS we probably need a hybrid: per-region customer-managed keys (preferred), plus a KMS-proxy for customers who want control-plane managed keys. Also need per-request attestation that control-plane issued the header and which KMS was used.

jeff: Metrics we should capture: cutover start -> routing header propagated (should be <5s), active connections drained (should be measurable; aim <2m), failed requests during cutover, and % of retries. These will help set SLOs.

rachel: I'll draft the RFC PR with an operator-runbook. Proposed timeline: prototype (2w) -> internal canary (1w) -> gradual rollout (4w). I can own the PR. @anika @jeff fyi.

soren: great — please add legal/audit requirements too (anika). I'll open the PR and include these measurement goals + the KMS options. If no major objections, we proceed with prototype next sprint. :rotating_light:
